title: Fibrations between local objects are unchanged by left Bousfield localization
statement: Use model categories, simplicial model categories and derived mapping spaces as in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category and $S$ a small set of its arrows. Call an object $Z$ $S$-local when it is fibrant in $\mathcal M$ and, for every $(A\to B)\in S$, the map $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence. Here all derived mapping spaces are computed in the original model structure. Assume a model structure $L_S\mathcal M$ exists on the same underlying category, with the same cofibrations as $\mathcal M$, whose weak equivalences are exactly the arrows inducing equivalences of these derived mapping spaces into every $S$-local object. If $X,Y$ are $S$-local objects, then a morphism $p:X\to Y$ is a fibration in $L_S\mathcal M$ if and only if it is a fibration in $\mathcal M$. No properness or combinatoriality assumption is imposed.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Proposition 3.3.16(1), printed p. 63 (PDF p. 77). The source allows arbitrary model categories; the simplicial specialization fixes the derived mapping-space convention. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Write $C,W,F$ for the original classes and $W_S,F_S$ for the localized weak equivalences and fibrations. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the original derived mapping spaces are mapping spaces of the original infinity localization. Therefore $W\subseteq W_S$: precomposition by an equivalence induces an equivalence on mapping spaces into every $S$-local object. As the cofibrations are unchanged, $C\cap W\subseteq C\cap W_S$. Taking right lifting classes in the two model weak factorization systems gives $F_S\subseteq F$. This already proves the implication from localized to original fibration, without any condition on the endpoints.

source.place: Hirschhorn Proposition 3.3.3(1) and Proposition 3.3.16(1), printed pp. 58,63; the class comparison is expanded from the weak factorization axioms. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For each $s:A\to B$ in $S$, choose a cofibrant replacement $a:A_s\to A$ that is a trivial fibration, and factor $sa$ as a cofibration $t_s:A_s\to B_s$ followed by a trivial fibration $b:B_s\to B$. The cofibrations are a left lifting class, so their composition closure [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] makes $B_s$ cofibrant. For every original fibrant $V$, the commutative square $(a,b):t_s\to s$ has weak-equivalence vertical arrows. The derived mapping comparison [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] thus identifies its two locality tests up to equivalence. Hence $V$ is $S$-local exactly when each strict enriched map $m_{s,V}:=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B_s,V)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A_s,V)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. SM7 makes $m_{s,V}$ a Kan fibration between Kan complexes (the endpoints $A_s,B_s$ are cofibrant). By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], that condition is equivalently that $m_{s,V}$ be a trivial Kan fibration. No condition on the original $A,B$ was imposed.

source.place: Definitions 3.3.8 and Lemma 3.3.11(1), printed pp. 60-61: specialize the resolution construction to cofibrant arrow replacements and simplicial tensors. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
Put $\partial_n:\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$, and form
$$h_{s,n}:P_{s,n}:=(A_s\otimes\Delta^n)\amalg_{A_s\otimes\partial\Delta^n}(B_s\otimes\partial\Delta^n)\longrightarrow B_s\otimes\Delta^n.$$
These are original cofibrations with cofibrant endpoints. Here is the direct verification from SM7 in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. For any cofibration $i$ and simplicial-set monomorphism $j$, a lifting square from $i\mathbin\square j$ to an original trivial fibration $r$ transposes by tensor-Hom adjunction to a square from $j$ to the SM7 map associated to $(i,r)$. That map is a trivial Kan fibration, and lifts against $j$ by the Kan model weak factorization system [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Thus $i\mathbin\square j$ is an original cofibration. Apply this first to $i:0\to A_s$ or $0\to B_s$ and $j:\varnothing\to K$, for any simplicial set $K$, to see that their tensors with $K$ are cofibrant; the tensor adjunction identifies tensors of initial objects with initial objects; apply it to $0\to A_s$ and $\partial_n$ to make $A_s\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to A_s\otimes\Delta^n$ a cofibration. Its pushout is $B_s\otimes\partial\Delta^n\to P_{s,n}$. Pushout and composition closure [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] now give cofibrancy of $P_{s,n}$, and application to $(t_s,\partial_n)$ gives the assertion for $h_{s,n}$.

source.place: Definition 3.3.8 and Proposition 3.3.9(1), printed p. 60; direct SM7/tensor proof of the simplicial horns and their cofibrant endpoints. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
Each $h_{s,n}$ is in $W_S$. Fix an original fibrant $S$-local $V$. Step 2 makes $m_{s,V}$ a trivial Kan fibration. Tensor-Hom adjunction and the universal property of the pushout in Step 3 identify $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(h_{s,n},V)$ with the corner map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\Delta^n,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B_s,V))\longrightarrow
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^n,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B_s,V))
\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\partial\Delta^n,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A_s,V))}
\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\Delta^n,\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A_s,V)).$$
A lift of a boundary $\partial_m$ against this corner is exactly a lift of $\partial_n\mathbin\square\partial_m$ against $m_{s,V}$, by the same adjunction. The former pushout product is degreewise the inclusion of the union of the two boundary products into $\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$, hence is a monomorphism. A trivial Kan fibration lifts against every monomorphism by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], so this corner lifts every boundary and is a trivial Kan fibration. Since both endpoints of $h_{s,n}$ are cofibrant, the strict mapping sets into fibrant $V$ compute derived mapping spaces by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Thus $\operatorname{Map}^h(h_{s,n},V)$ is an equivalence for every test $V$, as required. In particular Step 3 makes $h_{s,n}$ a localized trivial cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.10(1) and Lemma 3.3.13(1), printed pp. 60-61; expand the simplicial tensor/mapping-space calculation instead of presuming the localized model structure simplicial. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For an original fibrant $V$, Step 2 and the boundary lifting characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] give the following exact criterion: $V$ is $S$-local if and only if $V\to1$ lifts against every $h_{s,n}$. Indeed a square $\partial\Delta^n\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(B_s,V)$ over $\Delta^n\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(A_s,V)$ transposes to a map $P_{s,n}\to V$, and an extension to $B_s\otimes\Delta^n$ is exactly its filler. These identifications use the simplicial tensor-Hom adjunction of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], so hold also at $n=0$, when $h_{s,0}=t_s$. This is a locality test in the original structure, with no assertion that all local objects are localized fibrant.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.11(1), printed p. 61, with its lifting equivalence written explicitly for the chosen tensors. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Now let $p:X\to Y$ be an original fibration with both endpoints $S$-local, and factor it in the GIVEN localized model structure as $X\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{q}Y$, with $i$ a localized trivial cofibration and $q$ a localized fibration. Such a factorization is part of the model axioms [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; it uses neither small-object generation nor existence of any further model structure. Step 1 makes $q$ an original fibration, so $E$ is original fibrant: to lift an old trivial cofibration against $E\to1$, first extend its composite into fibrant $Y$, then lift that extension through $q$. For every $h_{s,n}$ and map $u:P_{s,n}\to E$, locality of $Y$ and Step 5 extend $qu$ to $v:B_s\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$. By Step 4, $h_{s,n}$ is localized trivial, so lift the square $(u,v)$ through the localized fibration $q$. This extends $u$ into $E$. Step 5 proves that $E$ is $S$-local.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.16(1), factorization on printed p. 63, and the expanded proof of Proposition 3.3.14(1), printed pp. 61-62. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: The arrow $i:X\to E$ is a local equivalence between $S$-local objects. In the original homotopy category, precomposition by $i$ is therefore bijective on maps into $X$ and into $E$. To justify this bridge explicitly, enlarge universes so that $\mathcal M$ is small. The class $W$ is a wide subcategory: identities have the left lifting property against every fibration, so belong to $C\cap W$, and two-out-of-three makes $W$ closed under composition. By [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], the reduced-hammock mapping simplicial sets represent the original localized mapping spaces, compatibly with actual maps and composition. The universal property in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies that localization with the one computing $\operatorname{Map}^h$. By [lem-coef-hammock-components-localization], their connected components are naturally the Hom sets in the ordinary formal-inversion localization $H=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$, with the same composition and actual-map functor $\gamma$. This formal-inversion category has the ordinary localization universal property: a functor inverting $W$ extends by sending each adjoined inverse $w^{-1}$ to the inverse of its image, and the composition and inverse relations are preserved. Surjectivity of $i^*:\operatorname{Hom}_H(\gamma E,\gamma X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_H(\gamma X,\gamma X)$ supplies $g$ with $g\gamma(i)=1_{\gamma X}$. Injectivity of $i^*$ with target $\gamma E$, applied to $(\gamma(i)g)\gamma(i)=\gamma(i)=1_{\gamma E}\gamma(i)$, gives $\gamma(i)g=1_{\gamma E}$. Thus $\gamma(i)$ is invertible. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] in the ORIGINAL model category, with no cofibrancy assumptions on $X,E$: $i$ is an original weak equivalence. Its original cofibration property follows from the shared cofibrations.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.13(1), printed p. 55, used in Proposition 3.3.16(1), printed p. 63; the local Whitehead argument is expanded through the existing model saturation theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Since $i$ is an original trivial cofibration and $p$ an original fibration, the old weak factorization lifting axiom [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] applied to the square with top $1_X$, bottom $q$, left $i$ and right $p$ gives $r:E\to X$ with $ri=1_X$ and $pr=q$. Hence $(i,1_Y):p\to q$ and $(r,1_Y):q\to p$ are arrow-category maps whose composite is the identity of $p$. By the right lifting class retract closure [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], $p$ is a localized fibration as an arrow retract of $q$. Together with Step 1 this proves both implications. No localized fibrancy of $X$ or $Y$ was used.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.16(1), printed p. 63; in this factorization the original-trivial-cofibration lift gives the required retract directly, expanding the concluding appeal to Proposition 3.3.15. Read online; not archived in literature/.
